clinician.trajectory_summary: A 56-year-old male presented with 6 years of disabling pruritus in a C6 dermatomal distribution, constant neck pain, and other neuropathic symptoms, which worsened with neck movement. Extensive prior workup ruled out dermatologic disease and peripheral neuropathy. Cervical spine MRI revealed notable spinal stenosis with early cord flattening at C3-4 and C4-5, and multilevel foraminal stenosis from C3 to C7. These findings correlated with his symptoms, leading to a diagnosis of neuropathic pruritus likely Brachioradial Pruritus (BRP) secondary to cervical compression. An ACDF from C3 to C7 was performed without complication. Four months postoperatively, the patient reported 95% improvement in symptoms, with only occasional pruritus.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with disabling pruritus and neck pain for 6 years, with symptoms in a C6 dermatomal distribution, worsened by neck movement.
Extensive prior evaluation ruled out dermatologic disease and peripheral neuropathy as causes for pruritus.
Cervical spine MRI showed notable spinal stenosis with early cord flattening at C3-4 and C4-5, and multilevel foraminal stenosis from C3 to C7.

The patient's chronic axial mechanical neck pain and bilateral upper extremity radiculopathy correlated with the degenerative and stenotic segments from C3 through C7, and pruritus was possibly caused by compression of nerve roots and/or spinal cord.
Surgical intervention with ACDF from C3 to C7 was planned to provide relief of pain and pruritus.
The planned ACDF procedure was performed without complication.
Four months postoperatively, the patient reported 95% improvement in preoperative symptoms, with only occasional pruritus.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Extensive evaluation by dermatology found no evidence of dermatologic disease (E001).
Extensive evaluation by neurology found no evidence of peripheral neuropathy (E001).
